title: Endpoint version surface and ownership wires
summary: Working notes + wireframe writeup for adding clearer version surface, ownership metadata, and deprecation/rollout cues to the model catalog and endpoint creation flow. Focus: reduce accidental breakage from model upgrades, make pin state discoverable in lists and cards, and give a lightweight path for endpoint owners to schedule deprecations and rollbacks.
goals: Make endpoint pin/version status immediately visible in catalog and endpoint lists
Expose ownership and contact info on endpoints to reduce noisy paging
Provide clear microcopy for pin actions and automatic fallback behavior
Create a lightweight deprecation scheduling UI (date + grace policy)
Minimize new clicks in common flows (create endpoint, pin version, rollback)
wireframe_descriptions: Three primary screens: 1) Catalog grid card: adds a compact version badge, last-deployed-version, 'pinned' toggle and small owner chip. Card hover reveals a tiny activity timeline (deploy, pin, last call). 2) Endpoint creation modal: two-column form. Left side: endpoint basics (name, route, payload schema). Right side: version policy block with radio options: 'always-latest', 'pin-to-version', 'managed-rollout'. If pin chosen, show searchable dropdown with model versions and an inline explain link. 3) Endpoint detail page: header shows endpoint owner, current active version, pin state, deprecation banner if scheduled. Secondary area: rollback button with one-click quick-rollback to last stable version and an advanced 'canary rollout' panel for percentage-based traffic shifts. Wires emphasize small status affordances (color + icon), minimal copy, and keyboard-accessible toggles.
copy_drafts: Catalog card badge: 'v3.1 (pinned)' — hover tooltip: 'Pinned by Priya Nair on 2025-09-02. Endpoint will not auto-upgrade.'
Pinned toggle in endpoint header: 'Pin endpoint to a model version' — help: 'When pinned, your endpoint stays on the selected model version until you unpin or manually upgrade.'
Version policy option: 'Managed rollout — Redwood will gradually shift traffic to a new version and monitor quality regressions.'
Deprecation banner (scheduled): 'This endpoint is scheduled for deprecation on 2026-04-01. Traffic will automatically switch to the fallback version after this date unless a new pin is set.'
Rollback CTA: 'Quick rollback to last stable (1 click) — Reverts traffic and restores previous keys.'

Create endpoint confirmation copy: 'Create endpoint — This will provision route <endpoint-name> and start serving the selected model version. You can change versioning policy anytime in Endpoint Settings.'
Empty states: 'No pinned endpoints yet. Pin a version to freeze behavior and avoid accidental upgrades.'
Tooltip for owner chip: 'Endpoint owner. Click to message owner or open runbook.'
Warning modal when unpinning: 'Unpinning will allow this endpoint to receive automatic upgrades. Are you sure? This may change latency and cost.'
Canary intro microcopy: 'Roll out a new model gradually. Start with 1–10% traffic, monitor latency & quality metrics, then increase.'
accessibility_notes: Ensure all status badges have text equivalents and aria-labels (e.g., 'pinned version 3.1'). Color alone should not indicate critical state — include icons and short text. Keyboard focus order must hit the pin toggle, owner chip, and rollback button in that sequence. Modals should announce context (e.g., 'Confirm unpinning of endpoint...').

decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decided to show 'pinned' at the card level rather than only in detail to reduce accidental upgrades. Tradeoff: more visual noise in catalog; mitigated by compact secondary text and hover details. Chose a discrete 'managed-rollout' option instead of auto-managed default to avoid surprise changes for customers with strict SLAs. Deferred full scheduling DSL for deprecation (we'll implement date + grace window in phase 1).
outstanding_questions: Should pin be tenant-scoped or org-scoped (current plan: org-scoped with project-level override)?
What metrics do non-Redwood customers want surfaced in early canary (latency, errors, embedding drift)?
Do we surface cost-estimate deltas when changing versions/pinning? (UX placeholder exists but backend support TBD)
